question: According to which of the following foreign travellers did Dhruvasena II attend Harsha’s assembly at Prayag (Allahabad)?
solution:
The correct answer is **Hiuen Tsang**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hiuen Tsang**, also known as Xuanzang, was a Chinese Buddhist monk, scholar, traveller, and translator who visited India during the reign of King Harshavardhana.
 
• He came to India in the 7th century (precisely around 630 AD) to acquire Buddhist texts and to study at the ancient university of Nalanda.
 
• Hiuen Tsang's detailed accounts provide valuable insights into the political, social, and religious life of India during this period.
 
• He attended the assembly at Prayag (Allahabad) organized by King Harsha, which was a significant religious gathering attended by scholars, monks, and dignitaries from different parts.
 
• His works, especially the **Si-Yu-Ki** or the **Records of the Western World**, are crucial sources of historical information not only about India but also about other regions in Central Asia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Aspect
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **Prayag Assembly**
 Organized by King Harsha, it was a grand religious gathering that attracted scholars, monks, and dignitaries, showcasing the religious tolerance and patronage of Buddhism.
 
 

 **Nalanda University**
 An ancient center of higher learning in Bihar, India, famous for its Buddhist scholarship but also taught other subjects.
 
 

 **Buddhist Pilgrimage**
 Hiuen Tsang's journey to India was part of a broader tradition of Buddhist monks travelling to gain knowledge and religious texts.
 
 

 **Translation Work**
 After returning to China, Hiuen Tsang dedicated his life to translating the Buddhist scriptures he had collected into Chinese, significantly influencing Chinese Buddhism.
 
 

 **Legacy**
 Hiuen Tsang is remembered for his contributions to the spread of Buddhism and for his detailed accounts that offer insights into medieval Indian history.
